requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: A pattern expression that is to be matched a number of times SHALL be followed by one of the postfixes "#(n, m)", "#(n, )", "#(, m)", "#(n)", "#n", "#(,)", "#()" or "+".
requirements.original: To specify that the preceding expression should be matched a number of times one of the following syntaxes shall be used: "#(n, m)", "#(n, )", "#(, m)", "#(n)", "#n", "#(,)", "#()" or "+".

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfix "#(n, m)" SHALL match the preceding expression at least n times and not more than m times.
requirements.original: The form "#(n, m)" specifies that the preceding expression shall be matched at least n times but not more than m times.

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfix "#(n, )" SHALL match the preceding expression at least n times.
requirements.original: The metacharacter postfix "#(n, )" specifies that the preceding expression shall be matched at least n times while "#(, m)" indicates that the preceding expression shall be matched not more than m times.

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfix "#(, m)" SHALL match the preceding expression not more than m times.
requirements.original: The metacharacter postfix "#(n, )" specifies that the preceding expression shall be matched at least n times while "#(, m)" indicates that the preceding expression shall be matched not more than m times.

ambiguity.issue: The lower bound of "#(, m)" is not stated; by analogy with "#(,)" being "#(0,)", 0 is assumed.
readings: The postfix "#(, m)" SHALL match the preceding expression 0 to m times.
The postfix "#(, m)" SHALL match the preceding expression 1 to m times.

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfixes "#(n)" and "#n" SHALL match the preceding expression exactly n times.
requirements.original: Metacharacters (postfixes) "#(n)" and "#n" specify that the preceding expression shall be matched exactly n times (they are equivalent to "#(n, n)").

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfixes "#(n)" and "#n" ARE equivalent to "#(n, n)".
requirements.original: Metacharacters (postfixes) "#(n)" and "#n" specify that the preceding expression shall be matched exactly n times (they are equivalent to "#(n, n)").

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: In the postfix form "#n", n SHALL be a single digit.
requirements.original: In the form "#n" n shall be a single digit.

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfixes "#(,)" and "#()" ARE shorthand notations for "#(0,)" and match the preceding expression any number of times.
requirements.original: The forms "#(,)" and "#()" are shorthand notations for "#(0,)", i.e. matches the preceding expression any number of times.

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfix "+" SHALL match the preceding expression at least 1 time.
requirements.original: The metacharacter postfix "+" denotes that the preceding expression shall be matched at least 1 time (equivalent to "#(1,)").

requirements.subject: ent:repetition-postfix
requirements.canonical: The postfix "+" IS equivalent to "#(1,)".
requirements.original: The metacharacter postfix "+" denotes that the preceding expression shall be matched at least 1 time (equivalent to "#(1,)").

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: A pattern notation "\N{reference}", where reference denotes a one-character-length template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter, matches the character in the referenced value or template.
requirements.original: A notation of the form "\N{reference}", where reference is denoting a one-character-length template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter, matches the character in the referenced value or template.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the reference in \N{reference} cannot be resolved
requirements.canonical: If the reference in a "\N{reference}" pattern notation cannot be resolved, the TTCN-3 tool SHALL generate an error.
requirements.original: If the reference cannot be resolved or if the referenced symbol is anything else than a template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter containing a character string of length 1, an error shall be generated.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.condition: the referenced symbol is not a one-character-length template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter
requirements.canonical: The reference in a "\N{reference}" pattern notation SHALL NOT denote anything other than a template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter containing a character string of length 1; otherwise an error SHALL be generated.
requirements.original: If the reference cannot be resolved or if the referenced symbol is anything else than a template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter containing a character string of length 1, an error shall be generated.

ambiguity.issue: Read together with "\N{typereference}" (next sentence), a reference to a charstring or universal charstring type is also allowed; this sentence lists only value-like symbols. The canonical text assumes the type form is an exception handled by B.1.5.4-s003.
readings: A "\N{...}" reference to anything other than a one-character template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter, including a charstring type reference, SHALL cause an error.
A "\N{...}" reference that is neither a one-character template, constant, variable, formal parameter or module parameter nor a charstring or universal charstring type reference SHALL cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: A pattern notation "\N{typereference}", where typereference references a charstring or universal charstring type, matches any character of the character set denoted by the referenced type.
requirements.original: A notation of the form "\N{typereference}", where "typereference" is a reference to a charstring or universal `charstring` type, matches any character of the character set denoted by the referenced type.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: A referenced character set that is not a subset of the values allowed by the type of the template or template field in which the pattern is used IS NOT an error.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Cases when the referenced set of characters is not a subset of values allowed by the type definition of the template or template field for which the character pattern is used, are not be treated as an error (but e.g. matching never can occur if the two sets do not overlap).

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: A "\N{...}" pattern whose referenced character set does not overlap with the values allowed by the type of the template or template field CANNOT match any value.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Cases when the referenced set of characters is not a subset of values allowed by the type definition of the template or template field for which the character pattern is used, are not be treated as an error (but e.g. matching never can occur if the two sets do not overlap).

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: The pattern notation "\N{charstring}" IS equivalent to "?" when applied to a template or template field of charstring type.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: \N{charstring} is equivalent to ? when the latter is applied to a template or template field of charstring type and \N{universal charstring} is equivalent to ? when the latter is applied to a template or template field of universal charstring type (but causes an error if applied to a template or template field of charstring type).

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: The pattern notation "\N{universal charstring}" IS equivalent to "?" when applied to a template or template field of universal charstring type.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: \N{charstring} is equivalent to ? when the latter is applied to a template or template field of charstring type and \N{universal charstring} is equivalent to ? when the latter is applied to a template or template field of universal charstring type (but causes an error if applied to a template or template field of charstring type).

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-character-set
requirements.canonical: The pattern notation "\N{universal charstring}" SHALL NOT be applied to a template or template field of charstring type; doing so causes an error.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: \N{charstring} is equivalent to ? when the latter is applied to a template or template field of charstring type and \N{universal charstring} is equivalent to ? when the latter is applied to a template or template field of universal charstring type (but causes an error if applied to a template or template field of charstring type).

ambiguity.issue: This contradicts NOTE 1 (B.1.5.4-s004), which says a referenced character set that is not a subset of the template type is not an error, and B.1.5.5, which allows universal charstring type references in charstring patterns only if all characters have corresponding charstring characters. The canonical text follows NOTE 2 literally.
readings: Applying "\N{universal charstring}" to a charstring template SHALL cause an error.
Applying "\N{universal charstring}" to a charstring template IS NOT an error (NOTE 1); it only matches the characters that also exist in charstring.

requirements.subject: ent:type-compatibility
requirements.canonical: A referenced type, template, constant, variable or module parameter of type charstring MAY be used in the pattern specification of a template or template field of universal charstring type.
requirements.original: For the purpose of referenced patterns (see clause 27.9) and references character sets (see clause B.1.5.3) specific type compatibility rules apply: a referenced type, template, constant, variable or module parameter of the type charstring always can be used in the pattern specification of a template or template field of universal charstring type; a referenced type, template or value of the type universal charstring can be used in the pattern specification of a template or template field of charstring type if all characters used in the referenced template or value and the character set allowed by the referenced type has their corresponding characters in the charstring type (see definition of corresponding characters in clause 6.3.1).

ambiguity.issue: "references character sets (see clause B.1.5.3)" refers to the referenced character sets of clause B.1.5.4; clause B.1.5.3 is "Match expression n times". Formal parameters, allowed as references in B.1.5.4, are not listed.

requirements.subject: ent:type-compatibility
requirements.condition: all referenced characters have corresponding characters in the charstring type
requirements.canonical: A referenced type, template or value of type universal charstring MAY be used in the pattern specification of a template or template field of charstring type only if all characters used in the referenced template or value, and all characters of the character set allowed by the referenced type, have corresponding characters in the charstring type.
requirements.original: For the purpose of referenced patterns (see clause 27.9) and references character sets (see clause B.1.5.3) specific type compatibility rules apply: a referenced type, template, constant, variable or module parameter of the type charstring always can be used in the pattern specification of a template or template field of universal charstring type; a referenced type, template or value of the type universal charstring can be used in the pattern specification of a template or template field of charstring type if all characters used in the referenced template or value and the character set allowed by the referenced type has their corresponding characters in the charstring type (see definition of corresponding characters in clause 6.3.1).

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether the check is on the actual characters used (value/template) or on the whole character set of the referenced type, and whether it is a compile-time or runtime check for variables and module parameters. "value" is used where the first half lists "constant, variable or module parameter". The canonical text requires both conditions.
readings: A universal charstring reference MAY be used in a charstring pattern if the characters actually used in the referenced value or template have corresponding charstring characters.
A universal charstring type reference MAY be used in a charstring pattern only if every character of the subtype character set has a corresponding charstring character.

requirements.subject: ent:nocase-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@nocase` modifier IS placed directly after the `pattern` keyword.
requirements.original: When the "@nocase" modifier is used after the pattern keyword, the matching is evaluated in a case insensitive way, i.e. at positions, where without the "@nocase" modifier a small letter alphabetical character would be matched, with the "@nocase" modifier also capital letter counterpart - but only that - shall be accepted.

requirements.subject: ent:nocase-modifier
requirements.condition: the `@nocase` modifier is used after the `pattern` keyword
requirements.canonical: When the `@nocase` modifier is used, a pattern SHALL also accept the capital letter counterpart at every position where it would match a small letter alphabetical character without the modifier.
requirements.original: When the "@nocase" modifier is used after the pattern keyword, the matching is evaluated in a case insensitive way, i.e. at positions, where without the "@nocase" modifier a small letter alphabetical character would be matched, with the "@nocase" modifier also capital letter counterpart - but only that - shall be accepted.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence only describes small letters additionally accepting their capital counterparts, while it also says matching is "case insensitive". It is unclear whether a capital letter in the pattern also accepts its small letter counterpart.
readings: With `@nocase`, a pattern SHALL accept both the small and the capital counterpart of every alphabetical character in either direction.
With `@nocase`, a pattern SHALL additionally accept only the capital counterpart of small letters; capital letters in the pattern do not match small letters.

requirements.subject: ent:nocase-modifier
requirements.canonical: When the `@nocase` modifier is used, a pattern SHALL NOT accept any character other than the matched small letter and its capital letter counterpart at that position.
requirements.original: When the "@nocase" modifier is used after the pattern keyword, the matching is evaluated in a case insensitive way, i.e. at positions, where without the "@nocase" modifier a small letter alphabetical character would be matched, with the "@nocase" modifier also capital letter counterpart - but only that - shall be accepted.

requirements.subject: ent:nocase-modifier
requirements.canonical: When the `@nocase` modifier is used, a pattern matching the character đ (latin small letter d with stroke) SHALL also accept Đ (latin capital letter d with stroke).
requirements.original: For example, at positions where the pattern matches the character đ (latin small letter d with stroke), also its counterpart Đ (latin capital letter d with stroke) shall be accepted, but the similarly looking graphical characters Ð (latin capital letter eth) and Ɖ (latin capital letter african d) shall not.

requirements.subject: ent:nocase-modifier
requirements.canonical: When the `@nocase` modifier is used, a pattern matching the character đ SHALL NOT accept the similarly looking characters Ð (latin capital letter eth) and Ɖ (latin capital letter african d).
requirements.original: For example, at positions where the pattern matches the character đ (latin small letter d with stroke), also its counterpart Đ (latin capital letter d with stroke) shall be accepted, but the similarly looking graphical characters Ð (latin capital letter eth) and Ɖ (latin capital letter african d) shall not.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-pattern
requirements.canonical: The case sensitivity property of a referenced pattern IS NOT inherited by the referencing pattern.
requirements.original: When referencing a pattern from inside another pattern (see clause 27.9), the case sensitivity property of the referenced pattern is not inherited.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-pattern
requirements.canonical: After dereferencing, possibly recursively, only the resulting string part of a referenced pattern IS inserted into the referencing pattern.
requirements.original: I.e. - after dereferencing, possibly recursively - only the resulting string part of the referenced pattern is inserted into the referencing pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:pattern
requirements.canonical: A pattern containing references IS evaluated as a whole according to the case sensitivity of the referencing pattern.
requirements.original: The whole resulting pattern is always evaluated according to the casesensitivity of the referencing pattern.
